original.verdict_vo: Real answer: number 8, because this animal's longest canines could reach 15 centimetres. Probably your best bet for keeping everything else away.

fact.text: Inostrancevia, a gorgonopsian, had large canines, the longest of which could reach 15 cm.
fact.source_sentence: It also has very advanced dentition, possessing large canines, the longest of which can reach 15 cm (5.9 in) and which may have been used to shear the skin of prey.

original.description: Long before dinosaurs, the top predators on Pangaea were sabre-toothed relatives of mammals. Eight Permian animals, from a shy burrower to the biggest gorgonopsian of all, and which one would really keep the night quiet.
original.related_topic_hint: Pangaea: One Night on Earth's Supercontinent

options.image_prompt: Close side profile of one small male Diictodon sitting at the entrance of a burrow in red earth. Its compact barrel-shaped body is supported by four short sturdy legs. The broad short head has a smooth pebbled leathery surface, small ear openings and a blunt curved horny beak. Two short pale canine teeth point downward from the upper jaw, one on each side behind the beak. The near cheek and near tusk are clearly visible in side profile. A short tapering tail rests on the earth behind its body. The animal looks out of the burrow, lit by soft moonlight; a single distant ember adds a restrained orange reflection. Rust-red Permian floodplain under a dusty violet night sky, neutral soft moon fill and a restrained warm ember accent, photoreal painterly natural-history reconstruction, vertical composition.

options.label: Tree-climbing Suminia
options.vo: Level two: Suminia, clinging to a branch.
options.image_prompt: Complete side view of one small Suminia crouching horizontally on TOP of a thick conifer branch. Its entire compact slender body, elongated neck, broad short blunt head and long tapering curling tail are visible. All four slender legs bend naturally at their joints, and all four feet grip the upper bark with long clearly separated toes. Its belly rests just above the branch and its head faces left along the branch. The long tail curves along the branch behind it. Small rounded scales, natural muted grey-brown skin, a large dark eye, a clearly closed mouth. The branch crosses the lower middle of the frame, with open violet sky behind and a warm ember reflection on the bark. Rust-red Permian floodplain under a dusty violet night sky, neutral soft moon fill and a restrained warm ember accent, photoreal painterly natural-history reconstruction, vertical composition.
options.art_direction: A small four-legged Suminia crouches horizontally on top of a conifer branch with every foot gripping the bark and its long tail visible against the violet sky

options.label: Tusked Dicynodon
options.vo: Level three: a beak and two great tusks.
options.image_prompt: One living Dicynodon in clear near-side profile, all four sturdy legs planted naturally on red earth. Its low broad barrel-shaped body has natural grey-brown wrinkled leathery skin and a very short tail. Its short broad head has a prominent smooth curved horny beak at the front. One long ivory canine tusk descends vertically from EACH SIDE of the upper jaw just behind the beak. The near cheek and downward tusk are fully visible. A smooth low rounded nasal ridge connects the beak to the forehead. It grazes sparse horsetail plants with its head held forward, lit by neutral moon fill and a restrained warm light on the near flank. Rust-red Permian floodplain under a dusty violet night sky, neutral soft moon fill and a restrained warm ember accent, photoreal painterly natural-history reconstruction, vertical composition.
options.art_direction: A low quadrupedal Dicynodon in near-side profile shows its curved horny beak and downward upper-jaw canine tusk while grazing sparse horsetails

options.vo: Level four: a walking tank of bony bumps.
options.image_prompt: One living Scutosaurus in a complete low side profile, standing on ALL FOUR short thick legs with its broad belly close to the ground. Low rounded bony knobs stud the skin of its broad back and flanks. Short blunt bony projections border the sides of the cheeks. Its small closed mouth has a blunt rounded muzzle. All four similarly sized weight-bearing feet are planted on the earth; the front legs and hind legs are equally sturdy. Natural grey-brown pebbled skin with a soft amber edge light.
